scope: Read-only source and existing evidence; no new model call, cloud sample, edit, test, or deployment
incident: Exact 0.2.566 non-admin guest-to-member first page question: mandate start 200, same-conversation tool_results 200, resume route entered, public ALB generated 504 at 59.999 seconds with no target headers. Later 0.2.567 run failed its resource guard before Chat and adds no discriminator.

source.comparison: Prior evidence compared the exact resume router, preparation function, streaming wrapper, pool/admission paths and found no repair in the newer deployed SHA. Current checkout inspection agrees with the reported call chain; no claim is made that checkout state is itself deployed.
source.response_gate: packages/matrx-connect/matrx_connect/streaming/response.py:1144-1199 awaits prepare_fn before creating/returning StreamingResponse; no total preparation deadline is applied
pre_response_stages: target resolution if omitted, answered-delegated check, outstanding-delegated read
spine run claim or legacy standalone coordinator claim
memory flag, request scope bind, conversation attribution restore, request-context tracking, COPPA check
conversation reconstruction; sandbox/run arm; orchestra tool resolution; context-block resolution
optional agent/context-policy and scope resolution; declined-write read; surface context; watch-frame attachment; context-object application; user-request ensure
dictionary and final-stage application after the claim-protection try
response construction and lane drain on refusal or construction failure
source.notable_code_risk: The try/finally that releases a claimed run covers only part of preparation; apply_dictionary and apply_final_stage are awaited after it. This is an objective claim-lifetime gap if either raises, but there is no evidence either failed or caused this 504. Do not present it as the incident cause.

existing_observability_limit: chat_timing marks prep_begin and prep_complete, but console emission is disabled by CHAT_TIME_CHECK_ENABLED=False. The timing summary/latency row is scheduled from the AI run finalizer, which cannot run before preparation returns; an in-flight 60-second stall therefore need not leave those records. API request_log records duration only when call_next exits. Existing CloudWatch route-entry log is not keyed to a usable per-await trace, and its concurrent DB exceptions cannot be assigned to this request. The supplied native report did not capture a request ID. Another generic API log sample cannot localize the await.
supported: The browser delivered the tool result successfully for this conversation; the backend accepted the resume route but returned no response headers to ALB within its 60-second limit.
Preparation contains numerous awaited DB/context operations before the StreamingResponse is returned; a pending one can explain the observed transport shape.
Database pool/connect/query failures occurred concurrently, including on the route-entry task, but the failed member await is not identified.
unproven: Which awaited function consumed the 60 seconds, whether it was DB/pool or another dependency, whether the server later completed, and whether the member-specific sign-in transition matters.
Whether unchanged backend behavior would now pass under different runtime pressure. The short post-deploy exception-free sample did not exercise the exact member flow.
next_minimal_diagnostic: On the backend, add one temporary structured span around prepare_resume_conversation with a private opaque request correlation key, monotonic elapsed time, phase name before/after each top-level await (group the pure local steps), and a finally record of last-entered phase, completion/cancellation, and elapsed time. Emit to bounded server logs independently of the run finalizer, sanitize IDs/payloads, and tag for removal. Include a mark after prepare_fn and just before return from create_prepared_streaming_response to distinguish preparation from response construction/drain. Only then perform one resource-valid exact member repro with passive transport capture and match its request correlation to the phase log. The first entered phase without exit is the next code boundary for a one-variable test; if all phases exit, investigate response handoff/middleware. No timeout, pool-size, or retry change is supported yet.
next_fix_test: Once the exact await is identified, build a red-capable test exercising that real dependency/interaction and showing the original pre-header stall; fix that origin, assert the response opens before the public idle deadline and the signed-in member receives an answer after Page Text. Retest the original guest-to-real-member transition and a fresh-direct-member control; check sibling continuation routes only for the confirmed pattern.

live_backend_delta_20bd_to_f8dd.verdict: The live backend is a changed deployment/environment, so one guarded original-member reproduction is meaningful for current symptom status. This delta supplies no concrete code repair to the known pre-response resume boundary. A pass would establish only that the symptom did not reproduce under the new conditions, not that f8dd fixed D261; a repeat 504 still needs request-correlated phase timing.
live_backend_delta_20bd_to_f8dd.residual_uncertainty: Changed unrelated jobs/background work may alter runtime load, and a deploy restart may alter transient conditions; neither is a demonstrated cause or fix without a correlated repro.
